events.excerpt: Microsoft researcher and collaborator combine new mathematical ideas with human-directed AI to resolve a central problem in high-dimensional geometry and probability At a glance Fundamental scientific breakthrough: Researchers resolved the Kannan-Lovász-Simonovits (KLS) conjecture, a 31-year-old problem widely regarded as one of the central open questions in high-dimensional geometry, with implications for statistics, optimization, algorithms, and computer science. A universal geometric principle: The result establishes a universal geometric principle for log-concave distributions, showing that simple flat cuts can capture their narrowest bottlenecks within a fixed factor, regardless of dimension. Human-AI collaboration: The breakthrough emerged from a human-directed agentic research process in which AI systems explored mathematical possibilities while researchers evaluated, pruned, and redirected the search. Independent confirmation: Multiple independent researchers have validated this research, identifying its central criterion as the key breakthrough, followed by a machine-checked formal verification. events.excerpt: This post follows Informed Diffusion: making home builders publish fast (2026). Author: @cskiraly Update, 29 October 2026: this post stays as published. Its text is kept current, with the latest results, on notes.ethereum.org , and each version, with its data and scripts, at eth-networking-studies . SEACAST’s specification and its releases are at informed-diffusion-spec ; news is posted as replies to this topic. TL;DR Ethereum has more and more large objects to broadcast, and little time for each. Today’s payloads are small and datacenters carry them, which is much of why mainnet is in time, but payloads grow (with gas increase and block-level access lists, BALs) and timelines shrink (with quick slots). Execution proofs and consensus blocks with post-quantum signatures may soon join the large-message club too. Today’s delivery method (gossipsub) sits far from being optimal : every node waits for the whole object before passing it on, and receives several copies of it. From a builder at home, the last nodes receive a 1 MiB payload seconds late. Not every node needs every byte. With data-availability sampling, a node is to receive its samples of an object, not the object. PeerDAS’s 128 column topics are only one way of doing sampled diffusion; RowDAS and FullDAS are other examples.
events.headline: SEACAST: fast, lean, sampled broadcast for Ethereum, with an executable spec and a formal model

events.excerpt: Today, we are expanding our web application firewall (WAF) by adding two new capabilities: full transaction detections and response rules. Full transaction detections evaluate each HTTP request alongside its response to identify evidence of exploitation. It helps answer both "Does this request look malicious?" and "What happened when the application handled it?" Response rules can then block the origin’s response before it reaches the requester. These are valuable protections because the latest frontier models are uncovering vulnerabilities buried deep in widely used software, giving defenders clarity on what to fix — and attackers new paths to exploit. The recent php2shell vulnerability shows the stakes: a flaw in a common software component can put applications across the Internet at risk. AI agents scanning for vulnerabilities can be extremely persistent, adapting payloads using feedback, and chaining vulnerabilities, credentials, and permissions. An application's response can reveal whether an attempt worked and give an attacker information that helps them go deeper. Inspecting incoming requests remains essential for stopping recognizable attacks before they reach an application. But some threats become clear only when the request is considered alongside what the origin retur
events.headline: Introducing full transaction detection for Cloudflare WAF

events.excerpt: Opening community discussion on URC-5: Token Venue Policy . Some tokens recommend particular liquidity pools or restrict trading to supported venues, often because their mechanics depend on a Uniswap v4 hook (INDEX, STANDARD, FWA, etc). Without a shared way to discover those policies, routers and frontends need token-specific integrations and may otherwise offer unsupported routes. Anecdotally, STANDARD and FWA prevented a lot of trading volume due to routers routing to restricted pools and required bespoke integrations for both. URC-5 defines IVenuePolicy , a token-level interface for declaring canonical v4 pools, distinguishing Preferred and Enforced policies, and exposing directional permissions for other liquidity venues. It also specifies how routers, aggregators, and frontends should interpret those declarations. Transfer-time enforcement remains token-specific. We’d appreciate input from hook developers, token teams, routers, aggregators, and frontend implementers. 6 posts - 4 participants Read full topic
events.headline: URC-5: Token Venue Policy

events.excerpt: Reth v2.8.0 schedules the Amsterdam hardfork on Hoodi, adds opt-in snap/2 sync and prewarm result reuse, and hardens peer-to-peer networking and RPC. With the opt-in --engine.prewarm-reuse , reth commits prewarmed transaction results instead of re-executing them. This reduced mean latency by 12.35% and raised Mgas/s by 18.58% over 500 replayed blocks ( #27894 ). Per-block proof-worker sizing reduced mean execution time on 300M-gas BAL blocks by 8.41% ( #27196 ). RPC response compression no longer cuts throughput by up to 22x ( #27863 ). Action Required Hoodi operators must upgrade before 26 October 2026 at 17:42:48 UTC. This release schedules Amsterdam on Hoodi at timestamp 1793036568 (epoch 132352) and extends the Hoodi fork IDs through Amsterdam. ( Reth change , Hoodi schedule ) All operators should review the default and behavior changes under Breaking Changes, especially those affecting the gas price oracle, WebSocket origins and the minimum priority fee. Update Priority User Class Priority Payload Builders Medium Non-Payload Builders Medium Breaking Changes Runtime and Configuration Changed the default gas price oracle ignore threshold ( --gpo.ignoreprice ) from 0 to 2 wei to match Geth, so zero-tip transactions no longer pull eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas down to 0. At the conclusion of the program, the agency asked White to prove the value of his work—on the ground. In this episode, Principal Technical Program Manager Weishung Liu talks with White, director of Catalyst Lab at Microsoft Research, about his unexpected break from academic research to help lead advanced tech operations in Afghanistan and his later decision to again work on tech with immediate, real-world implications: dark-web search tools used to help combat human trafficking. Liu and White explore the influences that led to these experiences plus the important role of problem selection in innovation and remaining hopeful after seeing the darkest parts of humanity. events.excerpt: In collaboration with @winderica TLDR: we port Tornado Cash to Flock, a post-quantum binary-field SNARK, proving a depth-32 withdrawal over SHA-256 in under 30 ms, and describe a simple recovery protocol, requiring only that wallets derive note secrets from a seed, that lets existing pools survive a discrete log break. Introduction Privacy pools such as Tornado Cash rest on the hardness of the discrete logarithm, through both their Pedersen commitments and their Groth16 proofs. Recent autoresearch efforts, both at lowering quantum resource estimates and at breaking hash functions , suggest that quantum discrete-logarithm circuits with far lower gate counts than the published ones, and yet-undiscovered attacks on the hash functions these pools use, may already exist. Recent progress in binary-field proving systems, ZCash’s deployment of ZIP 2005 in Ironwood, and the leanVM aggregation work all point the same way: privacy pools should now start to transition their stack to battle-tested cryptographic primitives. In this post we demonstrate a working Tornado Cash-like pool built on Flock : a plausibly post-quantum transparent hash based binary-field SNARK. events.excerpt: Hey Cosmonauts, I’ve been exploring an idea for a privacy-focused Cosmos SDK chain and wanted to bring it here before going too far into implementation. The idea is called VeilRoute — a sovereign Cosmos blockchain that acts as a confidential settlement and asset-routing layer between IBC-connected chains. The problem I’m interested in is relatively simple: Cosmos has interoperability through IBC, but what if applications could route assets through a common privacy layer without publicly exposing every internal transfer, amount, balance, or ownership relationship? I’m not proposing changes to the Cosmos Hub or requesting governance funding. This is an early architectural discussion to get technical feedback from people working on Cosmos SDK, IBC, ZK systems, and interchain security. 1. The idea Imagine a user moving ATOM from Cosmos Hub to Osmosis. Today, the public source and destination transactions are observable, along with the relevant IBC packet information. With VeilRoute, the proposed flow would be: Cosmos Hub / Other IBC Chain | IBC Deposit | v +---------------+ | VeilRoute | | | | Shielded Pool | | ZK Validation | | Private Notes | | Audit Records | +---------------+ | IBC Withdrawal | v Destination IBC Chain Users would deposit an IBC asset, shield it into a private not

events.excerpt: Should the Cosmos Hub have its own price oracle? CosmWasm is now permissionless on the Hub, but there is no price oracle available to contracts. Pyth dropped CosmWasm, SEDA is EVM-only, and Band over IBC is slow and costs fees on every query. Without prices, we can’t build any advanced defi on the Hub. So these apps get built on chains like Injective or dYdX, and ATOM ends up used everywhere except on its own chain. Idea: integrate an enshrined oracle based on the Slinky fork. Validators would publish prices at every block, secured by the Hub’s own validator set, with no dependency on an external provider. And beyond the Hub: these prices could be distributed over IBC to any connected chain that lacks an oracle. The Hub would become an interchain’s price provider, with fees flowing back to ATOM stakers. Longer term: prices are only the first step. The same validator-voted mechanism could later carry other data the interchain needs, such as LST exchange rates, proof of reserves or other verified off-chain data. The Hub would become the interchain’s trusted data layer. The Community Pool could fund the development and audit. Would you support this direction? Validators, would you be willing to run an oracle sidecar? 20 posts - 7 participants Read full topic

events.excerpt: At a glance A new form of computing . Zero-knowledge proofs let you run a workload and receive, alongside the result, a short proof that the program ran correctly. Anyone can check the proof in milliseconds, without rerunning the program, without trusting whoever ran it, and without needing data on which the program was run. Three grand challenges have stood in the way of broad adoption : making proofs fast enough to produce, making them available to normal programs without cryptographic expertise, and resting them on cryptography that will still be trusted many decades from now. Magnetar makes major progress on all three challenges. It proves programs written in Rust, Go, or C, runs 10 to 39 times faster on average than the prior fastest comparable systems, and rests its security only on standard hash functions. It is the latest result of more than a decade of research at Microsoft Research on making zero-knowledge proofs practical. A new form of computing Every result a computer produces comes with an implicit question: did the program run as claimed and produce correct outputs? Today, answering that question often requires a degree of trust alongside verification. We trust the operator, the vendor, the counterparty, or the agent, and we rely on contracts, audits, and logs to e

Ltd., a Major Payments Institution supervised by the Monetary Authority of Singapore, and by Paxos Issuance Europe Oy under the supervision of the FIN-FSA and in compliance with MiCA. Learn more at globaldollar.com and the https://arbitrum.io/products/usdg-vaults Builders drive the demand for onchain dollars. The Arbitrum Stablecoin Growth Program is designed to support the teams that bring that demand to Arbitrum. Protocols that make USDG their preferred stablecoin, collateral or on-ramp asset on the Arbitrum Platform can access incentives and ecosystem support to help them grow, without the cost and complexity of issuing their own stablecoin.
